strategy.summary: Reproduce the silently wrong Atom.grad for cvxpy.atoms.matrix_frac when X has more than one column. The buggy line vectorizes DX with DX.T.ravel(order='F'), which equals row-major DX.ravel(order='C'). The developer's regression test adds a MultiVarAtomConfig 'matrix_frac_matrix_x' with X shape (3,2) and P shape (3,3) psd to cvxpy/tests/test_grad.py, which runs a finite-difference gradient check. Run that test in the pure-Python cvxpy checkout at the buggy commit b5a20484ff95 (installed editable), then at the fixed commit (DX.ravel(order='F')). The transition is the success criterion.

pinned_because: NumPy >= 2.0.0 is a documented constraint (README.md), relied on as documented, not era-inferred
SciPy >= 1.13.0 is a documented constraint (README.md), relied on as documented, not era-inferred

No era ceiling is recorded for any dependency, so no upper pins are applied

strategy.reproducing_test: cvxpy/tests/test_grad.py: the new MultiVarAtomConfig entry 'matrix_frac_matrix_x' (lambda x, P: cp.matrix_frac(x, P) with variables [('unrestricted', (3,2)), ('psd', (3,3))]) run through the existing finite-difference gradient harness, which compares Atom.grad against a numerical gradient for X and P.
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision b5a20484ff95 the test matrix_frac_matrix_x fails: the finite-difference check for the matrix X gradient reports a max error of about 0.97 and the assertion trips. On the fixed revision (DX.ravel(order='F')) the same test passes with a max error of about 1.85e-08. The pre-existing matrix_frac vector-X case passes on both revisions because a transpose of a column vector is a no-op.
strategy.numerical_probe: Evaluate cp.matrix_frac(X, P) with X of shape (3,2) and a random symmetric positive-definite P of shape (3,3), then compare the Atom.grad output for X with a central finite-difference gradient of tr(X^T P^-1 X). The expected gradient is (P^-1 + P^-T) X in column-major order.

input_output_examples.input: matrix_frac with matrix X of shape (n, p), p > 1; finite-difference check of gradient

risks: The bug only appears when X has more than one column; the vector-X variant in the existing test file will not reveal it, so the new entry must be the one that selects the transition.
The bug affects Atom.grad only. problem.backward() and problem.derivative() use diffcp and are not affected, so tests through those paths will not transition.
The dtype, numeric precision and the exact tolerance of the regression test are not stated in the evidence. The pass/fail boundary depends on that tolerance, which is unknown here.
The test selection with -k matrix_frac may also pick up other matrix_frac tests; that is harmless but slows the run.
The test harness is assumed to call Atom.grad directly and to use a finite-difference comparison as the PR describes; if the harness differs, the failure signature will differ.
No platform, architecture or sanitiser dependence is stated, so the transition is expected on any platform that runs pure-Python cvxpy. Nothing here relies on a specific compiler or BLAS backend.
The buggy commit and the fixed commit must differ only in matrix_frac.py for the transition to be attributed to this fix; the PR diff suggests this but it is not independently confirmed.

oracle.reference_source: central finite-difference gradient inside the existing test_grad.py harness
oracle.why: The gradient is compared against a numerical reference. The PR reports error of about 1.85e-08 after the fix versus about 0.97 before, but the exact tolerance used by the test is not stated.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The finite-difference comparison for X sees a max error of about 0.97 because the buggy row-major ravel scrambles the gradient entries for the 3x2 matrix, so the assertion fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With DX.ravel(order='F') the gradient matches the finite-difference reference to about 1.85e-08, which is within the harness tolerance, so the test passes.
